subject: spanish
promptStrong: Give me a 40-word writing task in Spanish on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer for accuracy and range.
promptWeak: Give me a two-way translation drill (Spanish↔English) on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, with answers and the common mistakes to avoid.

questions.q: How do you say “I take after my mother”?
questions.explain: “Parecerse a” = “to look like / take after”, so “Me parezco a mi madre” = “I take after my mother”.

questions.q: What does “quedar con mis amigos” mean?
options: To stay home from my friends
To say goodbye to my friends
To meet up with my friends
questions.explain: “Quedar con” means “to meet up / arrange to meet”, so “quedar con mis amigos” = “to meet up with my friends”.
'Mayor' means 'older/elder', so 'mi hermano mayor' = 'my older brother'. 'Menor' would mean younger.
'El éxito' is a false friend: it means 'success', not 'exit' (which is 'la salida').
'Embarazada' is a classic false friend: it means 'pregnant', not 'embarrassed' (which is 'avergonzado/a').

questions.q: What is celebrated at “las Fallas” in Valencia?
options: Huge sculptures are built and then burnt
questions.explain: At “las Fallas” giant papier-mâché figures (“ninots”) are displayed and then burnt in March.
'La asignatura' is a false friend: it means 'school subject', not 'signature' (which is 'la firma').

questions.q: How would you write 'trabajador' to describe a hard-working woman?
questions.explain: Adjectives ending in -dor add -a for the feminine singular, so a hard-working woman is 'trabajadora'.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'I went to the cinema yesterday'?
options: Ayer iba al cine a menudo
questions.explain: 'Fui' is the preterite of 'ir' (I went); with 'ayer' the completed past is correct: 'Ayer fui al cine'.

questions.q: How do you say 'We celebrate my grandmother's birthday'?
options: Celebramos la Navidad de mi abuela
Celebro el cumpleaños de mi abuela
Celebramos el cumpleaños de mi abuelo
Celebramos el cumpleaños de mi abuela
questions.explain: 'Celebramos' = 'we celebrate' and 'de mi abuela' = 'my grandmother's', so the first option is correct.

questions.q: What does 'Es un buen amigo en quien puedo confiar' mean?
options: He is a friend who lies to me
He is a good friend whom I can trust
He is a friend I argue with
He is a friend I rarely see
questions.explain: 'Confiar en' means 'to trust', so the sentence means 'He is a good friend whom I can trust'.

questions.q: How would you write 'limpio' to describe two beaches ('playas')?
questions.explain: 'Playa' is feminine, so the plural adjective is feminine plural: 'limpias'.
Temporary states use 'estar': 'Estoy cansado'. 'Casado' means married, a near-miss spelling distractor.
